task_specification.objective: Advance release convergence by restoring dense, readable authored-cemetery presentation without replacing the authoritative map, qualifying bounded dense-wave performance behavior, and making one ordinary successful run through Result and Retry repeatable with authored upgrade-choice hierarchy and complete input focus.

diagnosis.root_cause: The preserved authored cemetery package loads and its camera-occlusion repair is working, but shipped-camera composition remains sparse, flat, and low-contrast, with weak landmark/depth layering and warm-versus-cool hierarchy. The remaining release gaps also require bounded dense-wave runtime behavior and a directly replayable successful Result→Retry lifecycle.

stop_conditions: Preserve the single AuthoredCemeteryPackage/CemeteryGarden instance and its native streets, collision, navigation, spawn lanes, landmarks, external depth, and verified camera-occlusion repair.
Do not replace or surgically modify imported source assets, add proxy roads/floors, or expand into unrelated backlog gaps.
Stop after the three bounded task families are implemented and host recapture can directly verify the required runtime and visual predicates.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different root-cause strategy from prior transform tuning: retain the authored package and repair presentation through additive composition/readability controls, while enforcing dense-run budgets and explicit lifecycle ownership/reset invariants in the authoritative runtime and UI state paths.

code: Run focused source/static checks for AuthoredCemeteryPackage singleton usage, native collision/navigation anchors, dense-profile caps and reset receipts, terminal single-commit invariants, and upgrade delta filtering/focus wiring.
Run the candidate’s existing automated checks for native Godot boot/project integrity and gameplay state transitions.
runtime: Host/Tester's recapture covers spawn, critical route, central landmark, and perimeter during ordinary movement and movement replay, including collision, boundary, external-depth, and disappearance/occlusion checks.

Host stress-tests three dense final-wave cycles at the target viewport, verifies frame/physics sample availability, active-count budgets, renderer/preflight provenance, runtime logs, and reset isolation after death, Result, Retry, and reload.

Tester executes one ordinary successful route through all waves and boss to Result, then player-caused Retry into a fresh run; verify exactly one terminal commit and no stale nodes, overlays, input locks, or duplicate callbacks.
visual: Compare same-framing gameplay captures against the bound Mournlight reference: denser cemetery composition, readable landmark silhouettes, layered depth, warm/cool lighting hierarchy, clear escape lanes, and compact HUD.

Inspect a live level-up draft and Result page at native/windowed/fullscreen UI scales for silhouette-first hierarchy, truthful current→new deltas, restrained copy, authored panels/icons, and complete keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus states.

done_when: The shipped cemetery reads as a denser authored moonlit garden with layered foreground, midground, and perimeter depth, grounded human scale, warm lantern versus cool moonlight hierarchy, readable escape lanes, and no visible primitive stand-ins or empty finished-art planes.
If native bounds require it, expand to a larger traversable scale without replacing native streets or adding a proxy floor; preserve a coherent external world/external depth around the playable area.

The central building/central landmark and all three landmarks remain readable during ordinary movement and movement replay, with aligned collision and navigation, no pass-through, no disappearance or occlusion drift, and a stable perimeter/boundary.
A focused recapture can verify spawn, critical route, central landmark, and perimeter views at the acceptance resolution with no visible void or support clutter.
tasks.instructions: Repair the candidate’s existing authored cemetery scene and spatial binding. Keep CemeteryGarden/AuthoredCemeteryPackage as one authoritative runtime instance with its native streets, terrain, buildings, props, materials, and landmarks. Add only bounded product-owned composition layers such as depth framing, restrained foliage/prop accents, value separation, and warm/cool light shaping around the package; do not duplicate, hide, extract, or reposition native child meshes. Rebase additive anchors to native geometry and preserve camera cull-envelope, spawn-lane, navigation, and collision contracts. Verify ordinary movement and movement replay around the central building/landmark and boundary/perimeter before handoff.
tasks.title: Restore dense authored cemetery composition and spatial integrity

done_when: Representative final-wave stress keeps active enemies within the authored 25–40 range and bounds projectiles, pickups, effects, lights, audio voices, navigation/steering work, and presentation updates without unbounded per-frame allocation.
Three-cycle dense profiling records nonzero frame and physics samples, active-count metrics, renderer/preflight provenance, and deterministic prepare→advance→reset receipts.

Death, Result, Retry, and scene reload return pooled enemies, pickups, effects, timers, signals, and audio ownership to baseline with no stale callbacks, duplicate spawns, leaked nodes, or persistent processing.
No new Godot/GDScript errors, invalid freed-instance access, NaN movement, or recurring error spam appear during the stress replay and reset cycles.
tasks.instructions: Inspect the existing dense-profile contract, RunController sampling, EncounterSpawner pooling, and WaveDirector pressure paths. Repair only proven hot-path or teardown defects: retain deterministic token-bucket scheduling and editor-only tester entrypoints, cap active entities/effects/voices, reuse existing pools, avoid scene-tree scans and repeated allocations in sampled hot loops, and disconnect/reset timers/signals/process owners on death, retry, and reload. Keep ordinary balance and release behavior unchanged when profiling is disabled. Expose bounded counters and reset-isolation receipts for host stress recapture.
tasks.title: Bound dense-wave cost and lifecycle cleanup

done_when: One ordinary non-diagnostic route advances from Title through warmup, all authored waves, boss telegraph/two phases/defeat, victory, and a single committed Result state.

Result presents victory/failure summary, build summary, Retry, and Title with stable focus; activating Retry starts a fresh authoritative run and clears transient combat, wave, draft, HUD, audio, pooled-entity, input-latch, and terminal-owner state.
The first-run guidance remains short, contextual, dismissible, and non-reappearing on retry; automatic combat and all three weapon identities remain intact.

Upgrade choices lead with authored weapon/upgrade silhouettes or icons, compact stat icons, and no more than three truthful current-to-new decision-relevant deltas; unchanged, exhaustive, locked, or placeholder rows are omitted. Keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus/hover/unavailable/selected states are distinct, debounced, and readable at configured viewport/UI scales.
tasks.instructions: Trace and repair the authoritative RunController state machine together with UpgradeDraftController/UpgradeDraftView and RunShellView. Make terminal ownership single-shot, ensure the successful ordinary route—not a diagnostic fixture—reaches victory Result, and preserve the existing terminal handoff/animation leases. Make Result→Retry reset ordering explicit and repeat-safe, including pause/input context, audio director, wave director, spawner pools, weapon runtimes, draft transactions, HUD, and first-run guidance. In the draft UI, retain authored icon assets and implement the required choice visual hierarchy with truthful current/new values and complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus behavior; do not turn cards into text-stacked data tables.
